advice: Propose a distinct four-tile K-pair unroll for the full512 NN kernel. Keep the same 32×32 output block, ZA0.S–ZA3.S accumulators, operand loads, pointer strides, and FP32 accumulation order. In both K loops, process K in pairs: load A/B operands for k and k+1 into separate vector registers, then issue the four FMOPA instructions for k followed by the four for k+1. Use a one-step cleanup only if the loop supports odd K; the generated 512 path has an even K extent. Preserve the existing row-major mapping, packing, stores, SME transitions, fallback, ABI, and license notices. The hypothesis is that fewer loop-control operations may improve throughput; any gain is unverified. This is distinct from the measured two-step unroll, which changed the same loop schedule but was described with a different load/compute order. The source review must confirm that this proposal changes the actual instruction schedule rather than merely renaming that prior experiment. Checks: verify each ZA tile receives k values in ascending order; inspect compiler output for register pressure or spills; check full overwrite and numerical tolerance on fresh inputs, general sizes, tails, and n≤0; then run ten validation reports and ten fresh alternating paired controls with unchanged settings and the frozen best-of-three rule. Report both historical and fresh same-mode peak comparisons. Do not promote without the existing paired threshold and held-out check.
risks: The prior measured two-step K-loop unroll had mixed paired results and was not promoted. This proposal may therefore be a redundant alias unless its source-level load and FMOPA schedule is demonstrably different. Additional live vectors may increase register pressure, and any reduction in loop-control cost may be offset by scheduling or code-layout effects. No performance benefit is established by the supplied evidence.
